nodes.title: the Hobnak signature
nodes.statement: The Hobnak system concerns objects called rastvashs. There are exactly 5 of them: lumpyr, lumnyr, opalbra, rastumb, fexrast. One operation is written ?. One relation is written >>, read as "supports".

nodes.title: the Hobnak combination tables
nodes.statement: The value of x ? y for every pair of rastvashs is fixed by the table of the first operation. The pairs standing in the >> relation are listed in full.

nodes.title: closure under the first operation
nodes.statement: For all rastvashs x and y, x ? y is again a rastvash.

nodes.title: reflexivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For every rastvash x: x >> x.

nodes.title: antisymmetry of the relation
nodes.statement: For all rastvashs x and y: if x >> y and y >> x then x = y.

nodes.title: transitivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For all rastvashs x, y, z: if x >> y and y >> z then x >> z.

nodes.title: agreement of the relation with the first operation
nodes.statement: For all rastvashs x, y, z: if x >> y then (z ? x) >> (z ? y) and (x ? z) >> (y ? z).

nodes.title: the system does not have association of the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all rastvashs x, y, z: (x ? y) ? z = x ? (y ? z).

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = lumnyr, y = lumpyr, z = lumnyr, left = lumpyr, right = lumnyr, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all rastvashs x and y: x ? y = y ? x.

nodes.title: pyrglim rastvashs
nodes.statement: A rastvash x is called pyrglim when x ? x = x.

nodes.title: rastvashs that vintzam
nodes.statement: Two rastvashs x and y are said to vintzam when x ? y = y ? x.

nodes.title: umbclo collections
nodes.statement: A collection S of rastvashs is umbclo when x ? y belongs to S for every pair x, y drawn from S.

nodes.title: the iskespa of a rastvash
nodes.statement: The iskespa of a rastvash x is the collection of rastvashs y for which x >> y holds.

nodes.title: the iskvor
nodes.statement: The iskvor of the system is the collection of rastvashs that vintzam with every rastvash.

nodes.title: the zamxil
nodes.statement: The zamxil is the collection of all pyrglim rastvashs.

nodes.title: the tarntarn of a rastvash
nodes.statement: The tarntarn of a rastvash x, written [x], is the smallest umbclo collection that contains x.

nodes.title: a kelddri
nodes.statement: A rastvash f is a kelddri when f >> y holds for every rastvash y, that is, when the iskespa of f is the whole system.

nodes.title: the vexnyr of a rastvash
nodes.statement: The vexnyr of a rastvash x is the number of rastvashs in its tarntarn [x].

nodes.title: the lumovi
nodes.statement: The lumovi of the system is the collection of rastvashs whose vexnyr is largest.

nodes.title: umbnyr pairs
nodes.statement: Two distinct rastvashs x and y form a umbnyr pair when x >> y and y >> x both hold, that is, when each lies in the iskespa of the other.

nodes.title: the tarntarn of a rastvash is umbclo
nodes.statement: For every rastvash x, the collection [x] is umbclo.

verification.domain: every object, then every pair inside its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is built by taking x and closing under ?.
Closing under an operation is exactly the sealing condition.
The carrier is finite, so the closure stops after finitely many rounds.

nodes.title: the tarntarn is contained in every umbclo collection
nodes.statement: If S is umbclo and contains x, then S contains all of [x].

verification.domain: every sealed collection against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every member of [x] is reached from x by finitely many applications of the operation.
A sealed S containing x is closed under each of those applications.
So each member of [x] is in S, by induction on the number of applications.

nodes.title: a rastvash is pyrglim exactly when its vexnyr is one
nodes.statement: x ? x = x holds if and only if [x] contains x alone.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: If x ? x = x then {x} is already closed under ?.
So [x] = {x} and the vexnyr is one.
Conversely a span of one object must contain x ? x, which is then x.

nodes.title: where the vexnyr divides the number of rastvashs breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every rastvash x, the vexnyr of x divides 5.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = lumnyr, reach = 2, size = 5, read straight from the tables.

nodes.title: the zamxil is umbclo
nodes.statement: If x and y are both pyrglim then so is x ? y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the ridge
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y be pyrglim.
The claim asks whether (x ? y) ? (x ? y) returns x ? y.
Whether it does is settled by running the operation table on every such pair.

nodes.title: iskespas are nested along the relation
nodes.statement: If y lies in the iskespa of x, then the iskespa of y is contained in the iskespa of x.

verification.domain: every ordered triple
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y satisfy x >> y and let z satisfy y >> z.
Transitivity gives x >> z.
So every member of the iskespa of y is a member of that of x.

nodes.title: there is at most one kelddri
nodes.statement: No two distinct rastvashs can both be kelddris.

verification.domain: every candidate against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let f and h both be floors.
Then f >> h, since h is any object, and h >> f likewise.
Antisymmetry forces f = h.

nodes.title: the relation survives combination on the right
nodes.statement: If x >> y then (x ? z) >> (y ? z) for every rastvash z.

verification.domain: every ordered triple
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y lie in the iskespa of x.
Compatibility applies the operation to both sides at once.
Nothing else is needed, since z was arbitrary.

nodes.title: no umbnyr pairs exist
nodes.statement: No two distinct rastvashs lie in each other's iskespa.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose x and y form a tight pair.
Antisymmetry then identifies x with y.
So a tight pair of distinct objects cannot arise.
